feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior-level communications CV with clear domain focus, credible progression, and relevant technical depth. It reads polished and substantive, but impact would improve with tighter formatting, fewer repeated skill sections, and more quantified outcomes beyond scope/responsibility.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility.  
- Strong positioning for digital strategy/communications leadership: web, CMS, analytics, multimedia, governance, and advocacy are all well aligned.  
- Writing is generally clean, professional, and specific; metrics like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views” add impact.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics in each role: e.g., growth percentages, engagement improvements, cost savings, efficiency gains, campaign performance, or team size/budget managed.  
- Fix style consistency issues: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience” (missing “of”); standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); consider consistent capitalization for “full-time” and date abbreviations (“Sept.”/“Oct.”). No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it is slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and foregrounding leadership in digital transformation will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your strongest differentiators: digital strategy leadership, platform modernization, and mission-driven/public-sector communications.
- Trim broad channel lists unless needed for ATS; emphasize outcomes and organizational complexity instead.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows/systems” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list overlaps with multiple experience bullets; consider keeping the intro more positioning-focused.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Digital strategy & transformation” → “Enterprise digital strategy,” “Multi-channel communication” → “Cross-channel communications leadership.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items for clarity; suggested version: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems & workflow design • Cross-channel communications leadership • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia, livestream & event production
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; “communication” should be “communications” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider dropping “Workflow & systems architecture,” which reads vague unless supported by architecture-specific examples.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header (“cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” “workflows and systems”).
- Also duplicates Topline Skills categories; if both remain, this section should be shorter and more high-level.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, standardized, optimized.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and publishing systems for coordinated cross-team communications.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content models, and user discovery experience.
- Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, reduction in turnaround time, engagement lift, search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo prior NACo roles, so emphasize what is new in this current engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team/operating leadership, and measurable business impact over channel lists.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Rewrite bullets to stress outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for email/social/video/analytics: subscriber growth, engagement lift, reporting speed, production cost savings, or reduced reliance on vendors after launching the in-house studio.
- Combine softer bullets for concision: merge governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning into one operational-improvement bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one at strategic/organizational level, not day-to-day execution.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep the CV item focused on leadership and capacity created.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational ownership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning, cross-team coordination and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations…” is very close to the Director role’s opening; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership/value angle and use tighter phrasing that reflects recent enterprise-scale work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging for mission-driven organizations
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Consider dropping “leadership” from the heading or shortening to “Digital Strategy & Content Operations” for concision.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing broad concepts with soft descriptors like “audience-focused.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale already proven in experience (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Core Competencies (“Digital governance & editorial systems,” “Multi-channel communications operations,” “Advocacy and public-sector communications”).
- “Enterprise digital strategy” is already implied in the header summary.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

items.aiFeedback:

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”

- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and migration” instead of just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid listing the same platforms verbatim in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or shorten here.

items.title: University of Virginia

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either sharpen platform depth or be condensed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of just names: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it feels lighter than the rest and may dilute seniority.
- Keep naming consistent with the CV’s impact language; “enterprise Drupal” or “Drupal 10” would better align with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities.
- If both sections stay, use Topline Skills for strategic breadth and this item only for platform names with proficiency/context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value for a senior candidate.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Front-End & Implementation Tools” to better match the content and sound less junior.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one brief proof point tied to recent work, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight serverless functions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GitHub Actions may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” if you want this section purely implementation-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If you have proof points elsewhere, consider replacing one lower-value tool with a capability phrase: **Airtable systems • workflow automation • cross-team planning tools**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases too often.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and, if possible, signal enterprise-level use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/level to make it stronger without becoming a work-history bullet: **Enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency/relevance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding phrases like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy”; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- Be careful with “engagement” wording if you can’t support CRM/community outcomes elsewhere on the CV.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early digital operations, and concrete outputs rather than repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 concrete outputs or scale markers if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or frequency.
- Tighten the close to show people/process impact: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and establish repeatable production workflows across web, email, social, and video.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as the launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim broad phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around distinct contributions: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for county-focused programs and policy teams…”
- Make the podcast the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten multimedia language: replace “Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program and policy communications.”
- Add scope or outcomes if available: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or research/project outputs delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad digital/media responsibilities already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- “Multimedia production” and “digital content” are recurring themes elsewhere; keep this entry focused on innovation/research coordination + first podcast launch.
